name: Agralaur
description:
You hear it before you see it. At first like a distant heartbeat, then a haze of commotion at the edge of your hearing. Finally you round the last bend in the river or arm of the coast and the sounds resolve into the pulse of the surdo, the patter of pandeiro, the plucking of bandolim, and voices from the throats of hundreds of revelers. Day or night, the city is in a constant state of carnaval, here where the river meets the sea.

Long ago, the dwarves, having been driven from their homeland in defeat, built great works of stone on the banks of the estuary. But the weight of the buildings was too much for the marshy ground and the city slowly sank into the mire. Ashamed of their twice-lost honor, the dwarves built no more. They took to living on the beaches and loathing the tools and works of their forebears, which still cluttered their rude huts.

Time passed. Other parts of the world flourished. Passing traders gave the sad ruins a wide berth at first, but as they tilted and sank they seemed less imposing, and soon goods changed hands at sea level atop the once-high summits of the dwarves' great ziggurats. Then some fool decided to use the ruins as a foundation, and when that first house sank and flooded, they built a second floor to keep living in, then a third. Soon other fools followed suit, and as trade continued they became rich fools, and then all the fools of the world rushed in.

Agralaur today is a city that revels in impermanence. Just as today's mansions will be the wet basements of tomorrow's hawker market, the cares of today will be the hazy memories of tomorrow's hangover. By luck of geography, prosperity flows into the city without effort. Fortunes are made one day and spent the next. It is an ever-changing, ever-dying, ever-new chaos of celebration, mourning and commerce.

hooks.name: Lady Fûktûn
hooks.description:
From the moment you arrived in town, you've felt like you were being watched: in a crowd, alone in a room - doesn't matter. You've also seen strange things: freshly prepared food appears rotten until you take a bite of it, green slime oozes down the sides of buildings, the faces of strangers shift into the faces of demons until you blink.

Other people cannot see these things when you see them, but locals affirm that everyone sees strange things in Agralaur. They also generally attribute the strangeness to Lady Fûktûn.

They say she dwells somewhere in the half-drowned Dwarven city below the streets. None have seen her, but her agents - tall, imposing humanoid forms that appear to be made entirely of strips of multicolored cloth - are known to appear in merchants' shops on the edge of evening to purchase rare and precious goods with ample coin. Her hoard must be very great and very well-guarded.
hooks.gmNotes:
Lady Fûktûn is, of course, a beholder, who does indeed have a massive hoard in a large, half-flooded chamber deep beneath the living city.

The chamber can only be reached by traversing a maze of sewer tunnels and crumbling walkways over dark water teeming with horrors. These ways are guarded by the Lady's strange, mute agents - who are indeed made of cloth animated by her magic.

As for entrée into this realm of wet darkness, Our Heroes could perhaps transact with one of Fûktûn's agents in a profitable exchange, but then find themselves hounded by them each evening for objects of greater and greater rarity. Or perhaps the strange visions and troubling feelings that pervade the city begin to feel like a pull downward. Or maybe a local sewer guide is convinced they can lead a raid on the Lady's hoard undetected (whether or not they are actually working for Fûktûn herself is up to you).

However you proceed, should Our Heroes best the beholder in her lair, consider an epilogue in which strips of multicolored cloth wash up on the beaches intermittently for months.

hooks.name: The Beast Marshes
hooks.description:
Flanking the river mouth and the harbors of Agralaur is a vast expanse of brackish marshlands. From the river, tall grasses stand like palisades of lances, stones at their bases have the appearance of dented and ruined shields, and choked streams of blood-red mud eke out of these, the fearsome Beast Marshes.

Legends tell of an ancient beastmaster who collected monsters from every corner of the earth for his own grim sport. When he died, heirless, the unattended beasts broke out of his keep and now roam the marshes, devouring all that cross their path.
hooks.gmNotes:
This can be a straight-ahead quest to defeat some big, challenging monsters to get to some ancient treasure in the beastmaster's keep, or you can add some complications:

Perhaps upon arrival at the keep, it turns out that the beastmaster still haunts the place from the grave. Or perhaps some other Evil Force has taken up residence there, and has continued training and breeding the beasts for sport. Perhaps Our Heroes are made to battle the fiercest of beasts for the entertainment of the Evil Force and their flunkies. Perhaps there is some weakness or internal strife among these ill folk that Our Heroes can exploit to gain their freedom?

Or perhaps upon entering the Marshes, Our Heroes find a network of plank paths, held just above the waters by poles. Who built these? How have they survived in the Marshes all this time? Do they worship the beasts? Have they tamed them? Are the beasts real at all or something these people invented to protect themselves? What are they protecting?

In whatever case, consider placing other questing folk in the Marshes, in various states of injury and despair. Bonus points for odd couples: a fashionable, young, inexperienced knight and an older, competent, experienced squire, etc.

hooks.name: Diving Day
hooks.description:
As the new city and its chaos rose over the bones of the old, the Dwarves removed to a small tidal island just outside the city, which they dubbed Fim do Trabalho - "End of Labors." Here their long sulking softened into a luxuriant laziness, and they became happy with their reduced state.

Still, the works of their ancestors - which seem now overwrought and alien - clutter their huts, and so they have made an annual ritual of flinging these objects into the sea. They call it the Lançando, but the ever-enterprising city-dwellers call it simply "Diving Day."
hooks.gmNotes:
You can take this any number of directions.

For one, perhaps a scholar of ancient Dwarven works suspects that the Dwarves of Fim do Trabalho have in their possession some powerful object that could be dangerous if it were to fall into the wrong hands. Perhaps one or more of those wrong hands has persuaded the Dwarves to include that object in this year's Lançando, and perhaps those same wrong hands have hired a team of skilled divers to ensure that the object comes to them. Whether the instigating scholar themself should prove to be right- or wrong-handed is of course up to you.

For another, perhaps it is another typical Diving Day, with the typical crop of valuable artifacts making their typical, bubbling way toward the bottom of the estuary and into the hands of the typical crowd of divers. But perhaps one of those divers is wanted dead by some local crime lord. Perhaps they fear for their safety and are seeking protection, as underwater murders during the chaos of Diving Day are not unheard of. Perhaps it turns out that the typical diver is in fact in league with the crime lord and Our Heroes are framed for the gratuitous murders of several other divers... for the artifacts they carried? for other offenses?

In whatever case, Diving Day should be a wild, reckless affair, exacerbated by the illicit water-breathing street drug, Jacques. A visit among the Dwarves' beach colony on Fim do Trabalho should reveal that among them is a nascent magic tradition born of leisure: conchomancy, hadaka matsuri, water-walking capoeira, etc.
